candidate.answerReason: The intersection consists of two square pyramids sharing a base of area 1/2, each with height 1/2, for total volume 1/6.

methods.label: Identify two square pyramids
methods.explanation:
First determine the possible heights \(z\). The first inequality implies \(|z|\le1\), while the second implies \(|z-1|\le1\). Their common range is \(0\le z\le1\). In this range, \(|z|=z\) and \(|z-1|=1-z\), so the two inequalities become
\[
|x|+|y|\le1-z,
\qquad |x|+|y|\le z.
\]
Thus a horizontal section satisfies
\[
|x|+|y|\le\min(z,1-z).
\]
For \(0\le z\le1/2\), this is \(|x|+|y|\le z\). Its boundary in each of the four choices of signs for \(x\) and \(y\) is a straight line. The square sections grow linearly from the point \((0,0,0)\) to the section at \(z=1/2\), forming a square pyramid. The part above \(z=1/2\) is an equal pyramid with apex \((0,0,1)\).

Their common base has vertices
\[
\left(\pm\frac12,0,\frac12\right),
\qquad
\left(0,\pm\frac12,\frac12\right).
\]
Dividing this square along the coordinate axes gives four right triangles, each with legs \(1/2\). Its area is
\[
B=4\left(\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac12\right)=\frac12.
\]
Each pyramid has height \(1/2\). Their interiors are disjoint, and their shared base contributes no volume, so the total volume is
\[
V=2\left(\frac13\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac12\right)
=\boxed{\frac16}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\text{A}\).
